notes: Historical D&A is taken from the consolidated statement of cash flows line item “Depreciation and amortization” (not a segment D&A subtotal). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Historical capex is taken from “Purchases of property and equipment” (cash flow investing section). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

NWC construction (absolute, for history) is operational working capital excluding cash/short-term investments/marketable securities, and excluding current notes payable; it includes accounts & notes receivable, contract assets, inventory, prepaid and other current assets, and offsets against accounts payable, accrued liabilities, current deferred revenue, customer deposits, and other current liabilities. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

EBIT is modeled as GAAP “Income (loss) from operations” (includes stock-based compensation and any GAAP operating impacts). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

NOL balance is set to the disclosed tax-effect amount (“net tax benefit totaling $58.4 million”) from the income taxes note; it is not the underlying gross NOL asset base. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Comps EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, and P/E (NTM) were left null because consistent NTM (next-twelve-month) values were not available from the primary/official sources pulled for this build; peer selection is based on public-safety/enterprise workflow and AI adjacencies.

catalysts: Outperformance (or underperformance) of 2026 revenue growth versus the guided 27% to 30% range and the implied operating leverage. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))
Progress in software mix and premium adoption over time driving higher long-term margins. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Incremental product/platform expansion and successful integration of acquired capabilities into the Axon Evidence and emergency communications workflows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Axon is a technology company providing integrated hardware and cloud software solutions for public- and private-sector operational workflows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Software & services include cloud/SaaS for capturing, securely storing, managing, sharing, and analyzing evidence (e.g., Axon Evidence and AI-enabled productivity tools). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Connected devices include TASER CEDs, body cameras, fixed/in-car cameras, and related ecosystem accessories and warranties, designed to work as an integrated offering. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))
current_context: Management guided 2026 revenue growth of 27% to 30% and maintained an adjusted EBITDA margin target of 25.5%. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))

Company reiterated 2028 targets of approximately $6B revenue and ~28% adjusted EBITDA margin. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))

2025 is described as a low point for operating cash-flow conversion due to investments in inventory and collection timing, with expectations to move back toward a ~60% conversion level in 2026. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth uses management’s 2026 guidance range and tapers after 2028, consistent with a scaling hardware + recurring software ecosystem. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))

EBIT margin recovery is modeled as operating leverage as revenue scales and cost headwinds (tariffs/inflation) normalize, translating adjusted EBITDA expansion into GAAP EBIT. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))

D&A and capex are held as stable-to-slightly-declining % of sales to reflect scaling investment without assuming runaway reinvestment intensity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Working-capital intensity normalizes from the elevated 2025 NWC level, assuming inventory/prepaid dynamics revert toward a more typical range. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Tariff/inflation and supply-chain component cost volatility could pressure margins and delay EBIT recovery. ([filecache.investorroom.com](https://filecache.investorroom.com/mr5ir_axon/594/Axon_Q4_2025_Earnings_Call_Transcript.pdf))

Working-capital strain (inventory, receivables/contract asset timing, and deferred revenue dynamics) could reduce free cash flow conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

Regulatory, cybersecurity, and AI reliability risks in high-stakes public-safety use cases could increase costs or limit adoption. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))

valuation_summary: DCF inputs are grounded in Axon’s FY2025 GAAP income statement and cash flow statements (revenue, operating income/EBIT, depreciation & amortization, and purchases of property & equipment). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001069183/000162828026011360/axon-20251231.htm))
Terminal value uses Gordon growth with a conservative long-run growth rate and WACC inputs suited for a high-growth, public-safety technology profile.
Scenario overlays adjust only growth, margins, and capital/working-capital intensity modestly, reflecting realistic dispersion around execution and cost normalization.
